questions.question:

• Hidden *means something which not visible or we can say "apparent."*
 
• ***Apparent** - appearing as actual to the eye or mind.*
 
• ***Covered** - it basically means hidden.*
 
• ***Veiled** - having or wearing a veil or a concealing cover.*
 
• ***Concealed** - kept out of sight or hidden from view.*

Hence, **apparent** is the most suitable antonym.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

If he __tried__ he would have succeeded.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'had tried'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are three forms of conditional sentences :
 
• **Conditional 1:** ‘if+simple present, will future E.g.* If I find her address, I’ll send her an invitation.*
 
• ***Conditional 2:** ‘if+simple past, conditional 1' **(=would+infinitive) **E.g. If I found her address, I would send her an invitation.*
 
• ***Conditional 3:** ‘if+past perfect, conditional 2' **(=would+have+past participle) ** E.g. If I had found her address, I would have sent her an invitation.*

This is a **third** conditional sentence showing a condition that is possible to achieve, and so it has to be written in the same format. Thus **option 3 is the most suitable option** and it should be written as ***'If he had tried he would have__ succeeded.'***

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

Applications are **__invite to__** eligible candidates for the post of Vice-Principal in a reputed school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'invited from'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to grammar, we need to use 'the third form of the verb invited' after 'are' because 'are' is a linking verb and after the linking verb we usually use the adjective with this adjective 'invited' the correct preposition will be 'from' because 'it indicates the source or provenance' hence the source here is 'eligible candidates' so we need to use 'invited from'

**The correct sentence will be -** *Applications **are invited from** eligible candidates for the post of Vice-Principal in a reputed school.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The wonderful performance of the maestro left the audience ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Entranced'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• To understand the solution for the sentence given, let's have a look at the options given.
 
• The sentence given has few words which make the correct option the answer.
 
• The words are: Wonderful, performance
 
• **If the performance is 'wonderful', that means, it is not 'Puzzling' for the audience.** 
 
• **'Sleepy' and 'Hungry' are the words not related to the context of the sentence given. **
 
• **Option 1, 3, 4 will, eventually, be eliminated. **
 
• Coming to the second option, 'entranced'.
 
• **The meaning of the word 'Entranced' means 'to leave someone with wonder, in surprise and delight'. **
 
• 'Entrance' has other meanings too: 'to cast a spell' and 'to allow access to a place'. But these two will not be applicable in this sentence given. 

Thus and so, **the sentence with the correct word** will be: *The wonderful performance of the maestro left the audience entranced__. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• वाक्य के समाधान को समझने के लिए, चलिए दिए गए विकल्पों (options) पर नजर डालते हैं।
 
• दिए गए 'sentence' में कुछ शब्द हैं जो सही विकल्प (option) को उत्तर बनाते हैं।
 
• वो शब्द हैं**: 'Wonderful', 'performance'. अगर 'performance'** "अद्भुत" है, तो इसका मतलब है, यह दर्शकों** ('audience') के लिए "Puzzling" **नहीं है।
 
• **'Sleepy' और 'Hungry' **शब्द** 'sentence' **के संदर्भ से संबंधित नहीं हैं।
 
• इस प्रकार, **Option 1, 3, 4 **को निरस्त किया जाता है। दूसरे विकल्प, 'entranced' की ओर आते हैं।
 
• **'Entranced' **शब्द का अर्थ होता है** 'किसी को आश्चर्य, चौंकाने और खुशी से परे छोड़ना'**।** 'Entrance' के पास अन्य अर्थ भी हैं: 'जादू करना' और 'एक स्थान की पहुँच की अनुमति देना'.** लेकिन इन दोनों का इस दिए गए 'sentence' में लागू नहीं होंगे।

अतः, सही शब्द के साथ वाक्य होगा: **'The wonderful performance of the maestro left the audience entranced.' **का हिंदी अनुवाद होगा - **'मेस्त्रो के अद्भुत प्रदर्शन ने दर्शकों को अत्यंत प्रभावित कर दिया।'**
